text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Ten state-run companies are to be closed. The companies accumulated 7.5 percent of all Romania's economy losses.
- Romania's central bank (BNR) is to withrdraw banking licences from troubled private banks Dacia Felix and Credit Bank, said BNR's governor Mugur Isarescu.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania will receive $1.7 billion in loans from international lenders this year, Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara said.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania's Finance Minister and BNR governor signed a letter of intent for the resumption of International Monetary Fund credits.
- The labour conflict at the Roman SA truck factory calmed after a government committee had talks with the trade union. The government promised to provide orders for the truck maker, newspaper says.
ZIUA
- An group of U.S. investors in Romania told Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea that Romania needs improved customs services and a tax regime.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Half of Romanians say the economic reform programme will succeed, while 76 percent of the population are displeased with their living standard, an opinion poll showed.
- President Emil Constantinescu will meet leaders of the opposition Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) for talks on progress with reforms.
- A judge and lawyer were sentenced by the Bucharest court of appeal to six and four years in jail for forging documents in more than 100 court cases.
ADEVARUL
- The general prosecutor started procedures to lift the parliamentary immunity of PDSR MP Gabriel Bivolaru who is to be investigated for alleged frauds worth 80 billion lei.
- The nationalist Greater Romania Party and Socialist Labour Party signed an accord under which the two parties will form electoral alliances in the next local elections.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania's population dropped by 74,000 people in 1996 to about 22 million.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- There is no measles epidemic in Romania, say health authorities.
- The newspaper publishes a report by Romanian emigres with alleged obstacles to Romania's NATO integration. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
